title: Hourly poll fetches a trailing 24h window per tracked sensor
given: 5 tracked sensors; OpenAQ mocked
when: the hourly job runs at :20 UTC
then: one /sensors/{id}/hours call per sensor with datetime_from = now − 24h; all returned rows stored

title: Re-polling the same window is idempotent
given: rows for the last 24h already stored
when: the same response is ingested again
then: rows_new = 0, rows_revised = 0; no duplicate (sensor_id, period_end) in readings_current

title: A changed value is stored as a revision, not an overwrite
given: hour H stored with value 40
when: OpenAQ later returns 55 for hour H
then: a second row with a later ingested_at exists; the old row is kept; readings_current shows 55; as-of query before the revision shows 40

title: Missing hours are recorded as gaps, never interpolated
given: OpenAQ omits 3 hours in a window
then: no rows exist for the missing hours; the gap is detectable from timestamps

title: A late-arriving hour is stored and re-evaluated
given: hour H missing at the first poll
when: H arrives 10h later inside the trailing window
then: H is stored and the pipeline evaluates hour H, producing station_scores and decision rows for it

title: First run backfills up to 90 days
given: empty database
then: each sensor is paged back up to 90 days (≤ 3 pages of 1000); kind = 'backfill' in ingestion_runs

title: One sensor failing doesn't stop the run, and the next run recovers
given: OpenAQ returns 500 for one sensor
when: the hourly job runs, then runs again with the API healthy
then: run 1: status 'partial' with the error logged, other sensors ingested; run 2 fills the missed hours

title: Rate limits are respected
given: OpenAQ returns 429
then: the client backs off and doesn't retry immediately; ratelimit_remaining is recorded on the run

title: Half-hour-offset periods are stored as-is
given: an Asia/Kolkata station whose periods end at :30 UTC
then: period_end is stored at :30, not rounded; local hour-of-day is computed from the station timezone

title: EPA 2024 PM2.5 band boundaries
then: Good, Moderate, Moderate, USG, USG, Unhealthy, Unhealthy, Very Unhealthy, Very Unhealthy, Hazardous

title: NowCast weighting and validity
given: 12h series with known values, and one with 2 of the last 3 hours missing
then: matches the AirNow worked example to 0.1 µg/m³; weight is clamped at 0.5; returns no value when fewer than 2 of the 3 most recent hours are valid

title: A missing API key fails fast and is never logged
given: OPENAQ_API_KEY unset; separately, set
then: unset: a clear startup error and no API call made; set: the key value appears in no log line or error message

title: Every run writes an ingestion_runs row with freshness
given: a normal hourly run
then: the row has started/finished times, rows fetched/new/revised, newest_period_end, status and ratelimit_remaining

title: The clock tick decides even when no data arrives
given: a sensor publishes nothing for 2 hours
then: each user on that station gets a decision every hour: no_event · NO_DATA, trigger = clock

title: Held notices release at quiet-hours end without new data
given: a notice held overnight; no new readings after 05:00
then: one released notice is sent (after D3–D7 re-checks), trigger = clock

title: Invalid values are excluded
given: readings of −1 and 1200 µg/m³
then: excluded from scoring with DQ_INVALID; kept as evidence

title: Low-coverage hours are excluded from scoring
given: an hour with percent_coverage 60
then: excluded with DQ_LOW_COVERAGE; still shown for display

title: A stuck sensor is detected
given: the same value for 6 consecutive hours
then: excluded with DQ_STUCK

title: An isolated one-hour glitch never notifies
given: Mumbai fixture: 75 → 980 → 90 µg/m³
then: the 980 hour is DQ_SUSPECT; no spike fires from it; no notification is sent

title: A jumping newest hour is suspect until the next hour confirms or clears it
given: the latest hour jumps >3x and +20 over the previous one, with no t+1 reading yet
then: it is DQ_SUSPECT now; if t+1 falls back it stays DQ_SUSPECT, if t+1 stays high it is re-scored clean

title: No data freezes episodes
given: an open episode; the sensor goes silent for 5h
then: decisions are no_event · NO_DATA; the episode neither closes nor notifies; when data returns, the gap hours are evaluated in order

title: Too little history means no baseline
given: fewer than 72 clean hours in the 14-day window
then: no_event · NO_BASELINE; no station_scores computed for that hour

title: A gap over 3h resets short-term state
given: EWMA and CUSUM elevated before a 4h gap
when: the first hour after the gap is evaluated
then: EWMA is re-seeded, CUSUM = 0 and spike memory is cleared

title: A silent sensor closes its episode quietly after 24h
given: an open, notified episode; the sensor goes silent
then: at 23h the episode is still frozen; at 24h it closes with close_reason no_data_timeout and reason NO_DATA_TIMEOUT; no notice is sent

title: Hour-of-day baseline with shrinkage and floor
given: a synthetic 14-day series with a known diurnal shape and one sparse hour
then: m_h and s_h match hand-computed median/MAD; the sparse hour is shrunk toward all-hours by n/7; s_h ≥ 0.15

title: The station's typical band comes from its 14-day median
given: Delhi and Helsinki samples
then: Delhi typical = USG; Helsinki typical = Good or Moderate

title: A spike needs 2 of 3 hours
given: z = 4 for one hour, then normal; separately, z = 4 for two of three hours
then: the first case doesn't fire; the second fires 'spike'

title: A climb needs 3 hours above the EWMA bar and a rising slope
given: a steady climb pushing EWMA over 1.26 with slope_6h > 0.01
when: scoring and triggering run hour by hour
then: fires 'climb' on the 3rd consecutive hour above the bar, not before; slope_6h is in the evidence

title: Slow build-ups fire 'elevated' when spike and climb never do
given: z ≈ 1.5 held for many hours
then: spike and climb never fire; 'elevated' fires once the user's CUSUM > 8, then that CUSUM resets to 0

title: Elevated is ignored once the level has faded
given: CUSUM crosses 8 while EWMA < 0.5
then: 'elevated' doesn't count as a trigger

title: Clearing needs 4 calm hours and the typical band
given: an open episode; EWMA < 0.5 for 3h, then 4h; separately, calm z but band above typical
then: 3h doesn't close; 4h closes; band above typical blocks closing

title: The absolute floor is edge-triggered
given: NowCast crosses into alert_band for 2 of 3 hours, then stays there for 2 days
then: fires once on the crossing; doesn't refire while it stays in the band

title: Near-misses are recorded in the user's trace, never notified
then: the decision trace lists the near-miss with score and bar; no notification

title: The same absolute value is unusual in Helsinki but normal in Delhi
given: three hours at 25 µg/m³ injected into the Helsinki and Delhi series
then: fires in Helsinki; no trigger in Delhi

title: Deterministic decisions
given: the same readings and rules
then: identical station_scores, episodes and decisions (message wording excluded)

title: Live/replay parity
given: readings ingested hour by hour with realistic lag
when: compared with a replay of the same data as-known
then: decision outcomes and reason codes match hour for hour

title: A polling outage evaluates every missed hour
given: 5 polls missed; data published meanwhile
when: the next poll ingests all 5 hours
then: each of the 5 hours gets station_scores and decisions, in order

title: One label per event, by precedence
given: spike, climb and elevated all fire in the same hour
then: the event kind is spike; the trace lists all three; the message wording uses spike

title: A flat, high plateau is elevated, not climb
given: EWMA above the climb bar for 6h but slope_6h ≤ 0
then: climb never fires; elevated fires when the CUSUM crosses its bar

title: A high-sensitivity user hears about smaller deviations
given: a deviation with z = 3.0 for 2 of 3 hours
when: default and high (k = 0.75) users are evaluated
then: high fires (bar 2.625); default doesn't (bar 3.5)

title: A low-sensitivity user is spared borderline events
given: z = 4.0 for 2 of 3 hours
when: default and low (k = 1.25) users are evaluated
then: default fires; low doesn't (bar 4.375)

title: Normal-for-Delhi doesn't nag, but a jump into Very Unhealthy does
given: Delhi at USG for a week, then a crossing into Very Unhealthy
then: no repeated notices during the USG week; one notice on the crossing

title: The relevance floor filters harmless 'unusual'
given: Helsinki rises 3 → 5 µg/m³ (Good); separately 4 → 15 (Moderate)
then: the first is suppressed · BELOW_RELEVANCE; the second notifies

title: Station scores never depend on users
given: the same station evaluated with only default users, then with a high-sensitivity user added
then: station_scores rows are identical in both runs; only the trace of the high-sensitivity user shows lower bars

title: Zero-config users get working defaults
given: a user with no rules row
then: defaults are applied (sensitivity default, relevance moderate, quiet 22:00–07:00, pace 6h, budget 3/day) and recorded in the trace

title: Invalid rules fall back safely
given: rules with an unknown field, a bad band name and a bad cron
then: RULES_INVALID is logged; the previous valid version is used

title: Rules are versioned and old decisions stay explainable
given: decisions made under rules v1
when: the user changes rules to v2
then: old decisions still reference v1 and explain correctly; new ones use v2

title: Quiet hours hold non-severe notices
given: a Moderate-band episode opens at 03:00 local
then: outcome held · QUIET_HOURS_HELD with deliver_after = 07:00 local

title: Severe air breaks through quiet hours
given: a Very Unhealthy escalation at 03:00 local
then: sent immediately · SENT_SEVERE_BYPASS

title: Held notices collapse into one on release
given: 3 held candidates overnight for one user
then: exactly one notice describing the current state; reason HELD_RELEASED

title: A held notice expires if the episode ended unnoticed
given: an episode opens and closes during quiet hours with nothing sent
then: nothing is sent; HELD_EXPIRED is logged

title: The check-in speaks only when today looks worse than usual
given: check_in at 06:30; overnight bad vs typical; separately, an ordinary night
then: bad night: one SENT_CHECK_IN notice; ordinary night: CHECKIN_QUIET and nothing sent

title: The check-in stays quiet right after another notice
given: a notice was sent 4h before the check-in
then: CHECKIN_QUIET; nothing sent

title: Cron and quiet hours use station local time, including DST
given: Helsinki and Los Angeles users across a DST change; a Delhi user (UTC+5:30)
then: check-ins and quiet windows land on the right local wall-clock times

title: Users only hear about their own location
given: a Delhi episode; a Helsinki user
then: the Helsinki user gets no Delhi decisions or notices

title: The pollutant filter is respected
given: a rule with pollutants = ['pm25']
then: only pm25 station_scores are considered

title: Every layer writes its trace in order, stubs included
given: any evaluated hour
then: decisions.trace lists D1..D8 in order up to the terminal one, including stubs D5–D7, each with layer, passed, reason_code and values

title: The check-in wins over quiet hours and absorbs held notices
given: quiet hours 22:00–07:00; a notice held at 01:00; check-in at 06:30 with today worse than usual
then: one SENT_CHECK_IN notice mentions the overnight episode; the held notice is HELD_RELEASED into it; nothing more is released at 07:00

title: Six bad hours produce one notice, not six
given: a band stays Unhealthy for 6 straight hours
then: exactly 1 notice; the other hours are suppressed · DEDUP_SAME_BAND or EPISODE_CONTINUES

title: Escalating one band speaks again
given: notified at USG; later Unhealthy after the cooldown
then: SENT_ESCALATED

title: Wobbling within the same band stays quiet
given: notified at Unhealthy; value moves within Unhealthy
then: suppressed · DEDUP_SAME_BAND

title: The flap guard reuses the episode
given: an episode closes; a trigger fires 4h later
then: the same episode id reopens; no new 'opened' notice

title: Cooldown decays by doubling within an episode
given: consecutive eligible notices in one episode
then: required gaps are 6h, then 12h, then 24h; the gap resets to 6h after the episode closes

title: Daily attention budget of 3 non-severe notices
given: 4 eligible non-severe notices on one local day
then: the 4th is suppressed · DAILY_BUDGET

title: Severe escalations skip pace and budget
given: cooldown active and the cap reached; a Very Unhealthy escalation
then: sent · SENT_SEVERE_BYPASS

title: Recovery is only announced after a genuinely bad period
given: a 5h Moderate episode closes; separately, a 14h episode or one peaking at USG+ above typical
then: the first is suppressed · RECOVERY_NOT_WORTH_SAYING; the second is SENT_CLEARED

title: At most one notice per user per hour, by priority
given: escalated and check-in candidates in the same hour for one user
then: only the escalated notice is sent; the check-in candidate is suppressed · ARBITRATED_OUT (priority: escalated > opened > cleared > check-in)

title: State survives a restart
given: an open, already-notified episode with an active cooldown
when: the process restarts and evaluates the next hour
then: no duplicate 'opened' notice; cooldown_until is honoured

title: Budget is separate from pace
given: 3 non-severe notices today from two different episodes; a 4th candidate whose own episode is well past its pace gap
then: D4 PACE passes; D7 BUDGET suppresses it · DAILY_BUDGET

title: Notices read like a real phone notification
given: any sent notice from replay
then: ≤ 220 characters; plain sentences; no JSON; doesn't match the bare status pattern 'AQI is now <n>'

title: Exactly one next action
given: any sent notice
then: contains exactly one action from the catalogue; next_action is stored

title: Trend, spike and recovery notices cite past context
given: sent notices of those kinds
then: each cites at least one history fact (e.g. 'since 2am', 'worst since 13 Oct')

title: No invented facts
given: an LLM-generated body
then: every number and date in the body appears in the insight JSON; otherwise the template fallback is used

title: Works without an LLM
given: no LLM key, or the LLM call fails
then: a valid template message is produced; generator = 'template'

title: Bad LLM output falls back
given: the LLM returns 400 characters or omits the action
then: the template fallback is used; the failure is logged

title: Actions fit the person and the hour
given: a morning-runner persona; an opened trend at 06:00 local
then: the action relates to the run (e.g. skip or move it indoors)

title: Released notices describe the night and now
given: a notice released after quiet hours
then: mentions what happened overnight (e.g. the peak time) and the current state

title: Human review of message quality
given: 20 notices sampled across cities and kinds from a replay
when: a reviewer rates each against a rubric (natural, specific, past context, one action, not a status update)
then: ≥ 18 of 20 pass every rubric item

title: A decision row exists for every user and every hour
given: 24 hours of evaluation for 5 users
then: 120 rows, including no_event ones, each with trigger 'data' or 'clock'

title: Suppressed and held decisions are as complete as sent ones
given: a suppressed and a held decision
then: each has reason_code, a human-readable reason, the full trace and detection evidence

title: Explain any notice from stored data alone
given: a sent notification id
when: the explain endpoint or view is called
then: returns the readings window as known then, baseline snapshot, detector scores, rules version and the stage-by-stage trace

title: Debug a missing nudge
given: a user and a time window where they expected a notice
when: decisions are queried by user and time
then: the stage that stopped it and why is visible (e.g. COOLDOWN with the elapsed vs required gap)

title: Notification history export
given: a user with sent notices
then: a file with time, kind, body, next action and decision id for every notice

title: Replay never mixes with live
given: a live database and a replay run
then: every replay decision carries replay_run; live queries exclude them

title: Feedback is recorded and doesn't change config
given: a sent notice
when: the user marks it acted, dismissed or not useful via the API
then: a feedback row exists and shows in the decision view; user_rules is unchanged

title: Feedback on an unknown notice is rejected
given: a non-existent notification id
then: a 404-style error; nothing is stored

title: The harness runs on the shipped sample without an API key
given: OPENAQ_API_KEY unset
then: it completes and writes a report

title: The report has the agreed metrics
given: a completed harness run
then: per station and persona: caught, missed, false alarms, notices per week, median time-to-notify, plus near-misses next to each miss

title: Glitch fixtures produce zero notices from glitches
given: the Mumbai fixture
then: no notice is attributable to a DQ_SUSPECT hour

title: A known real event is caught
given: the Helsinki smoke episode on 24 Aug (~27 µg/m³ vs a ~4 baseline)
then: a sent or held decision within 6h of onset

title: The pipeline never reads the wall clock
given: a frozen injected clock far from real time
then: all timestamps derive from the injected clock; a static check finds no direct now() calls in pipeline code

title: Notification volume stays in the calibrated range
given: the default persona on the 90-day sample
then: ≤ 4 event notices per week (opened/escalated/cleared/released) and ≤ 5 including morning check-ins, per default-sensitivity user

title: Runs unattended in the hosted environment
given: the deployed service
then: 24 ingestion_runs rows with status ok or partial; freshness lag under 3h for active sensors

title: Secrets stay out of git and logs
given: the repository and service logs
then: no .env in git history; no key value in logs

title: Optional concept UI shows feeds, decisions and replay
given: the Next.js demo deployed on Vercel
then: each user's notification feed, the decision log with reasons, and replay are viewable (first to be cut if time runs short)

title: README explains the project and credits the data
given: the README
then: explains what, why and how; how to run; carries the OpenAQ and provider attribution line

title: Architecture and decision note exists
given: the docs folder
then: a note covers the architecture, key decisions and trade-offs, and links the specs

title: AI tooling transcript exported
given: the submission
then: the Claude Code session transcripts are included

title: Notification history included
given: the submission
then: the exported notification history from a replay and/or live run is included

title: Demo video recorded
given: the submission
then: a Loom or similar link walks through ingestion, a decision trace and notices

title: Reference labels are independent of the live detector
given: the sample plus the hand-label file
then: 'interesting moments' come from ruptures PELT plus hand labels (Mumbai glitches as negatives), never from the live detector's own output

title: The rule engine and detection spec is complete before build
given: docs/specs/S-C
then: it defines scores, triggers (spike/climb/elevated/floor/clearing), rule format, layer order D1–D8, episode lifecycle, meaningful change, pace, arbitration, budget, timing and harness labelling, consistent with the closed explainer
